newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa ends off 8-mth lows, under pressure.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa ends off 8-mth lows, under pressure.

text.p: London cocoa futures ended off their eight-month lows on Friday as lack of follow-through after an aggressive selling spree led to mild short covering, traders said.
"They (sellers) were looking for stops below 950 (on March) but that didn't come to fruition and sterling's retracement brought some short covering towards the end of the day," said one trader.
The benchmark March position ended at 949 stg a tonne, off seven on the day, after tumbling to a new contract low of 946 stg early.
This is the lowest for eight months on continuation charts.
The early raid was helped by a relatively low turnover of 3,862 lots as most of Europe was closed to observe All Saints Day.
Traders said the technically-sensitive 945 stg level could be put to test and trigger sell stops next week.
"Technically it looks week. 945 needs to be tested," said one.
Traders were disappointed by the market's close on Thursday as sterling's fresh advance against the dollar attracted pre-hedging interest and kept potential buyers away.
A softer sterling could allow a recovery but traders said with industry buying at a low ebb, upside potential was limited.
Chart analysts are looking for a close above 955 or 960 for a near term improvement in the outlook.
In the physical market, industry bought some beans and products this week but demand soon dried up when currency factors came into play.
